  Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20, City Council Members will be participating via

  - City Council meeting videos are live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city and available for
  viewing thereafter, and televised on Cox 33 and Frontier FiOS 38 on Wednesday and Friday following the
  meeting.

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone,

  speak using the call-in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the Council meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there

  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 885 6012 0790, Meeting Password: 066081
  Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the
  following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand"
  option at the lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which
  item on the agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MAY 26, 2020

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order by MAYOR SCHMITZ at 7:12 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s
Executive Order N-29-20.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Dev/Public Works Director David Wahba
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Administrative Analyst Jessica Slawson

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

NONE.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless
good cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
consideration will be voted on separately.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF requested that Item 5G (Equestrian Committee
  Minutes of May 11, 2020) be removed for individual consideration.

  CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-F and 5H APPROVED AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF MAY 12, 2020

  APPROVED.

C.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – MAY 2020

  APPROVED WARRANTS 62785 THROUGH 62824 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $174,819.23 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 050220 THROUGH
  050420; 61409, 61526, AND 61815 VOID; IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $328,447.54 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $503,266.77 WITH
  PROPER AUDIT.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
MAY 26, 2020
 D.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORT OF APRIL 2020

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT OF APRIL 2020

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

F.  PALOS VERDES PENINSULA REGIONAL EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS
  COMMITTEE AND REGIONAL LAW ENFORCEMENT COMMITTEE MEETING
  MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 13, 2020

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

H.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF MAY 18, 2020

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

REMOVED FOR INDIVIDUAL CONSIDERATION:

G.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF MAY 11, 2020

  Recommendation: Receive and File.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF inquired about the Committee’s discussion of the
  Mayor’s Breakfast Ride on July 4, 2020.

  Assistant City Manager Davis confirmed that the Equestrian Committee’s
  recommendation has since been considered by the Park and Activities
  Commission, and that staff was now waiting for updates to the Los Angeles County
  Safer at Home Order to determine whether or not social gatherings will be allowed
  and the event can be held.

  City Manager Grammer confirmed that the Mayor’s Breakfast Ride is an event that
  staff would be able to coordinate in a short amount of time, allowing staff to wait
  until closer to the event date before making the decision to cancel or move forward.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  MITCHELL, APPROVED AS FOLLOWS:

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL RECEIVE AND FILE THE EQUESTRIAN
  COMMITTEE MINUTES of MAY 11, 2020.

  There being no objection, MAYOR SCHMITZ so ordered.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

  Amy Hill, a Rolling Hills Estates resident, addressed the City Council to suggest that
  the Council consider enacting an immediate leaf blower ban in Rolling Hills Estates
  due to the heightened community concerns during the COVID-19 pandemic.

  MAYOR SCHMITZ explained that the Council is unable to comment on this
  discussion topic as this item is not listed on the published agenda. She suggested
  this item be considered by the Environmental Advisory Committee (EAC).

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF suggested this discussion be placed on the June 9 City
  Council agenda. COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL concurred.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN disagreed and did not feel the urgency of skipping
  the EAC was necessary.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
MAY 26, 2020
   COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL stated that there were two issues brought forth by
  the speaker: a health issue regarding the spread of COVID-19 by leaf blowers and
  an environmental issue of the emissions from gas powered leaf blowers. She
  suggested this be considered by the City Council due of the urgent health issue, and
  that the environmental concerns of gas-powered leaf blowers be considered by the
  EAC. MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN concurred.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN stated that the County of Los Angeles Department
  of Public Health (LADPH) regulates public health in the City of Rolling Hills Estates
  but agreed the environmental portion should be considered by the EAC.

  City Manager Grammer summarized the Council’s discussion, suggesting that the
  EAC consider the environmental portion of this topic, and that staff gather information
  from LADPH. This information can then be presented to the City Council along with
  the EAC recommendations.

  Assistant City Manager stated that staff is currently working to schedule an EAC
  meeting at the earliest availability of the members.

  CONSENSUS OF COUNCIL TO DIRECT STAFF TO SCHEDULE AN
  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING TO BE HELD BEFORE
  THE NEXT CITY COUNCIL MEETING ON JUNE 9 FOR THE CONSIDERATION
  AND DISCUSSION OF A BAN ON LEAF BLOWERS.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 731, AN ORDINANCE
  OF CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES ADOPTING A
  NEW CHAPTER 17.78 OF THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE
  PERTAINING TO THE PERMITTING OF SPECIAL EVENTS AND REPEALING
  MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPTER 5.64 REGARDING TEMPORARY USE PERMITS

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1) re-open the continued Public Hearing;
  2) take any public testimony; 3) close the Public Hearing; and 4) conduct the
  second reading and adopt Ordinance No. 731.

  Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL RE-OPEN THE CONTINUED PUBLIC
  HEARING.

  There being no objection, MAYOR SCHMITZ so ordered.

  MAYOR SCHMITZ called for public testimony. Public comment was invited via email,
  via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live Zoom Webinar as noticed
  on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms. No public
  testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  ZUCKERMAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  There being no objection, MAYOR SCHMITZ so ordered.

  City Attorney Davis noted that the fees were being discussed as directed by Council,
  and would be brought back in June as part of the Schedule of Fees and Charges.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
MAY 26, 2020
   COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF confirmed that the fees were not intended to raise money
  for the City, and would be affordable for residents.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  CONDUCTED THE SECOND READING AND ADOPTED ORDINANCE NO.
  731.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

  Full title of Ordinance No. 731 read aloud by City Clerk Pettit.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  PROPOSAL FOR PROFESSIONAL TRAFFIC ENGINEERING SERVICES FOR
  THE PREPARATION OF A LOCAL ROAD SAFETY PLAN (LRSP)

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the Task Order with Willdan
  Engineering, to provide professional traffic engineering services for the preparation
  of a Local Road Safety Plan (LRSP) in a not-to-exceed amount of $76,100, all to the
  satisfaction of the City Attorney.

  Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as
  per the agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF confirmed that Willdan applied for this grant on behalf of
  the City.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN expressed concern about identifying more
  locations than would be addressed.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL echoed MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN’S
  concerns and inquired about the potential exposure to additional liability by identifying
  problematic intersections and areas and not properly mitigating the issues identified.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF inquired if additional grants are available to fund
  additional locations, in which Director Wahba confirmed.

  Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba and City Attorney Davis
  explained that staff would work with Willdan to analyze each location on a case-by-
  case basis before finalizing the list.

  Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and
  during the live Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website
  and social media platforms. No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVED THE TASK ORDER WITH WILLDAN ENGINEERING, TO
  PROVIDE PROFESSIONAL TRAFFIC ENGINEERING SERVICES FOR
  THE PREPARATION OF A LOCAL ROAD SAFETY PLAN (LRSP) IN A
  NOT-TO-EXCEED AMOUNT OF $76,100, ALL TO THE SATISFACTION
  OF THE CITY ATTORNEY.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
MAY 26, 2020
 B.  LEAGUE OF CALIFORNIA CITIES “SUPPORT LOCAL RECOVERY” CAMPAIGN

  Recommendation: That the City Council direct staff to 1) add the City’s name to the
  League’s “Support Local Recovery” campaign; and 2) authorize the Mayor to send
  the attached letter to the Governor asking for his support to provide $7 billion in state
  funding to support critical local services and allocate CARES Act funding for all cities
  for COVID-19-related expenditures, and advocate to secure $500 billion in federal
  aid for all cities nationwide.

  City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL clarified that the $500 billion was nation-wide not
  only for California, and also noted that cities with populations under 500,000 should
  be included in this CARES package unlike the last one.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN echoed COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL’S
  comments, and expressed his disappointment that the League of California Cities
  and the letter itself did not mention that smaller cities were left out of the first CARES
  package. He suggested an amendment to the letter requesting a more equitable
  distribution of funds for all cities especially smaller and underserved communities.

  Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and
  during the live Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website
  and social media platforms. No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  DIRECTED STAFF TO 1) ADD THE CITY’S NAME TO THE LEAGUE’S
  “SUPPORT LOCAL RECOVERY” CAMPAIGN; 2) AMEND THE SECOND
  ACTION WITHIN THE LETTER TO INCLUDE [FOR ALL CITIES
  NATIONWIDE] REGARDLESS OF SIZE, BUT PARTICULARLY SMALLER
  CITIES WITH UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES; AND 3) AUTHORIZE
  THE MAYOR TO SEND THE LETTER TO THE GOVERNOR ASKING FOR
  HIS SUPPORT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

  MAYOR SCHMITZ summarized a letter received from the Mayor of the City of
  Carson, which addresses the $1 billion of financial assistance from CARES given
  to the City of Los Angeles and Los Angeles County. The letter is requesting that
  some of these funds be shared with other cities, and the City of Carson is
  requesting that the City of Rolling Hills Estates sign onto this letter.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF agreed with the letter, as did COUNCIL MEMBER
  MITCHELL.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN offered his concerns about funding being taken
  away from the Los Angeles County Department of Public Health, which serves our
  smaller cities.

  Discussion ensued regarding the County’s need for these funds within the Public
  Health Department and the likelihood of funds actually being shared with local
  cities.

  APPROVED AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADDITIONALLY, DIRECTED STAFF TO 1) SUPPORT AND ADD THE
  CITY’S NAME TO THE LETTER DRAFTED BY THE CITY OF CARSON
  REQUESTING THAT THE $1 BILLION OF CARES ACT FUNDING GIVEN
  TO CITY OF LOS ANGELES AND LOS ANGELES COUNTY BE SHARED
  WITH THE LOCAL CITIES.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
MAY 26, 2020
   AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

C.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM FROM MEETING OF MAY
  18, 2020 - 2020 HILLS ARE ALIVE RACE AGREEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council not enter into a contract with Michael Hogue
  Production for the 2020 Hills Are Alive Race, and to direct staff to coordinate and
  implement the event if it can be held in 2020.

  Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  Discussion ensued regarding the payment schedule for the production company if
  the event were to be held, the potentially low attendance and difficulties with getting
  sponsors due to the current situation.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF stated that she believed staff would be able to sufficiently
  publicize the event through social media.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN noted that Michael Hogue utilizes a contact
  database beyond those within the City.

  MAYOR SCHMITZ expressed her excitement for the opportunity for City staff to be
  innovative and creative if it were to host the event without this contract.

  Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and
  during the live Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website
  and social media platforms. No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER
  MITCHELL, APPROVED AS FOLLOWS:

  DIRECTED STAFF TO NOT ENTER INTO A CONTRACT WITH MICHAEL
  HOGUE PRODUCTION FOR THE 2020 HILLS ARE ALIVE RACE, AND
  TO DIRECT STAFF TO COORDINATE AND IMPLEMENT THE EVENT IF
  IT CAN BE HELD IN 2020.

  There being no objection, MAYOR SCHMITZ so ordered.

D.  ORDINANCE NO. 732 AMENDING AND RESTATING MUNICIPAL CODE
  CHAPTER 12.24 (PARK USE REGULATIONS) OF THE ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1) receive any public testimony; and 2)
  introduce Ordinance No. 732 for first reading which amends and restates Municipal
  Code Chapter 12.24 "Park Use Regulations."

  Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF inquired about the origination of the items listed under
  the Prohibited Activities and Items section of the previous and proposed ordinance.

  Discussion ensued regarding the items listed under the Prohibited Activities and
  Items section, specifically the prohibition of flags, as well as the specific discussions
  had by the Park and Activity Commission.

  Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and
  during the live Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website
  and social media platforms. No public testimony was received.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
MAY 26, 2020
   COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL expressed concern regarding the Prohibited
  Activities and Items section, the Pet Animals section related to leashes, and the
  potential of security deposits. She also noted a correction needed in section
  12.24.210 in the title, in which City Manager should be changed to Supervisor.

  City Attorney Davis explained that appeals allow for resolution of issues outside of
  court, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL.

  MAYOR SCHMITZ expressed concern that the direction and discussion of the Park
  and Activities Commission is not reflected in the amended and proposed ordinance.

  Discussion ensued about the prohibition of specific activities and items within the
  parks, versus prohibition “unless a permit is obtained”.

  City Manager Grammer suggested that staff make the Council’s suggested
  amendments to the proposed ordinance and bring back to Council, along with
  rationale justifying why certain items were included in the proposed ordinance.
